markscheme.html:
a

gravitational potential is the work/energy per unit mass in bringing a point mass from infinity to a point in space ✔ this work is negative since the force is opposite to the displacement
OR
gravitational force is attractive
OR
gravitational force does work
OR
work done to bring the mass from the point to infinity would be positive ✔
ALT1 MP1 ‘per unit mass’ or ‘per kg’ must be included.

b.i

the «minimum» speed of an object «at the surface of a planet» for the object to reach infinity/leave the gravitational field/escape the gravitational field. ✔

Do not allow ‘overcome the force of gravity’. Award [0] for answers that state orbit.

b.ii

Use of 'GPE at surface  + KE of probe = GPE at new height ' ✔  ✔ « so» height ✔
Award ECF for MP3 from incorrect use of 0.9 factor.

question.html:
a The gravitational potential due to an isolated point mass is zero at infinity. Explain why the gravitational potential at all other points is negative. [2]

b A probe is launched from the surface of a planet with a speed 0.9 vesc where vesc is the escape speed from the planet.

b.i State what is meant by escape speed. [1]

b.ii The radius of the planet is . Determine, in terms of , the maximum height above the surface the probe can reach. [3]
